question.value: Whether SiC$_2$ is a parent species or a daughter species in the circumstellar envelopes of carbon-rich AGB stars.

evidence.quote: Whether SiC$_2$ is a parent species, that is formed in the photosphere or as a by-product of high-temperature dust formation, or a daughter species, formed in a chemistry driven by the photodestruction of parent species in the outer envelope, has been debated for a long time.

findings_qualitative.value: SiC2 exhibits an annular, hollow shell-like distribution in AI Vol, RAFGL 4211, and II Lup, indicating it is a daughter species formed in the outer CSE.

evidence.quote: Here, we analyze the ALMA observations of four SiC$_2$ transitions in the CSEs of three C-rich AGB stars (AI Vol, II Lup, and RAFGL 4211), and found that SiC$_2$ exhibits an annular, shell-like distribution in these targets, suggesting that SiC$_2$ can be a daughter species in the CSEs of carbon-rich AGB stars.
The distribution in hollow rings of the three sources indicates that SiC$_2$ is formed in the star’s outer layer through chemical reactions.

findings_qualitative.value: Higher rotational quantum number transitions of SiC2 are distributed closer to the star than lower rotational quantum number transitions.

evidence.quote: Compared to transitions with low rotational quantum numbers, transitions with high rotational quantum numbers are distributed closer to the star.

findings_qualitative.value: The fractional abundance of SiC2 increases with increasing wind density in the three observed C-rich AGB stars.

evidence.quote: We found that the fractional abundance of SiC$_2$ increases with the increasing wind density in the three observed C-rich AGB stars.

claims.hypothesis: SiC2 is a daughter species formed in the outer circumstellar envelope of carbon-rich AGB stars rather than a parent species.
claims.experiment: Analyze ALMA Band 3 channel maps and zeroth-order moment maps of four SiC2 transitions in three C-rich AGB stars (AI Vol, RAFGL 4211, and II Lup) and compare the spatial distribution with the parent species SiO.
claims.result: SiC2 shows hollow ring/shell distributions around all three stars with spatial radii between 2.12e16 and 8.90e16 cm (>20 R_*), distinct from the compact central distribution of parent species SiO.
claims.finding: SiC2 exists as a daughter molecule in the CSEs of these C-rich AGB stars, formed in the outer envelope via photochemical reactions.

evidence.quote: The SiC$_2$ and SiO shown in Figure [3](#fig:3) represent the spatial distribution characteristics of the daughter species and parent species, respectively, exhibiting distinct hollow and compact structures.

In the analyzed observations of three sources, the SiC$_2$ spatial distribution range is about 2.12 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ - 8.90 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm. To sum up, combining the ring brightness distribution of SiC$_2$ obtained in this work, we confirm that SiC$_2$ is the daughter molecule in the CSEs of C-rich AGB stars.

claims.hypothesis: The fractional abundance of SiC2 in these C-rich AGB stars varies with circumstellar envelope wind density.
claims.experiment: Perform shell fitting in GILDAS and LTE rotational diagram analysis across the observed SiC2 transitions to derive excitation temperatures, column densities, and fractional abundances relative to H2.
claims.result: The derived fractional abundances f(SiC2) are 1.64e-8 for AI Vol, 4.62e-8 for RAFGL 4211, and 47.46e-8 for II Lup, corresponding to wind densities of 4.08e-7, 5.13e-7, and 7.91e-7 M_sun yr^-1 km^-1 s, respectively.
claims.finding: The fractional abundance of SiC2 increases with increasing wind density across the three observed C-rich AGB stars.

evidence.quote: We found that the fractional abundance of SiC$_2$ increases with the increasing wind density in the three observed C-rich AGB stars.

why_this_data.value: A 3 mm survey revealed abundant molecules in these three carbon-rich stars, and high-resolution interferometric observations from ALMA are required to sensitively detect their spatial distributions.

evidence.quote: A survey conducted by (cite: smith2015molecular) at the 3 mm band revealed that the three carbon-rich stars possess abundant molecules, and the sensitive detection of molecular spatial distributions relies on more advanced telescopes such as ALMA.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Treating SiC2 solely as a parent species in C-rich AGB stars, as done in previous single-dish studies and astrochemical models.

evidence.quote: In the previous astrochemical models of C-rich CSEs of AGB stars, SiC$_2$ is always treated as a parent species with an initial abundance of $\thicksim$ $10^{-5}$ (cite: li2014photodissociation; 2018A&A...611A..29M; 2022MNRAS.510.1204V). However, this study clearly shows that this species is a daughter species and therefore the chemistry of SiC$_2$ in the chemical models needs to be reinvestigated.

limitations_admitted.value: Because the upper energy levels of the observed transitions are close in temperature (11.23 to 19.22 K), the errors on the derived excitation temperatures and column densities are rather large.

evidence.quote: As the upper energy levels are close in temperature, the errors on the derived quantities are rather large.

limitations_admitted.value: The 4_2,2 - 3_2,1 transition was not detected in II Lup (possibly due to an anomalous 300x300 pixel map size in the archive data), and the rotational diagram fitting of II Lup was performed using only two data points, resulting in lower precision and no error estimation.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the data without signal detection only covered a map size of 300 $\times$ 300 pixels. We speculate that there may have been some unknown special circumstances during the observations that led to the absence of signal.
The fitting of II Lup was performed using only two data points, which resulted in a lower precision and the absence of error estimation.

limitations_admitted.value: More sensitive observations may detect SiC2 emission at low levels in the inner CSE.

evidence.quote: More sensitive observations may, of course, detect SiC$_2$ emission at low levels in the inner CSE.

referee_caveats_inferred: The 12 m array observations with baselines 21-783 m lack short-spacing (ACA or total power) data, which could affect the recovery of extended emission in the CSEs, though a compact central parent component would not be resolved out.

Using LTE rotational diagrams over a very narrow upper-state energy range (11.2-19.2 K) yields poorly constrained excitation temperatures (e.g., 17.25 +/- 13.07 K in RAFGL 4211) and sub-thermal values (4.12 K and 6.66 K) that may indicate non-LTE excitation.
A minor numerical discrepancy exists between the text (f(SiC2) = 1.55e-8 for AI Vol) and Table 3 (1.64e-8, which is 0.90e13 / 5.52e20 = 1.63e-8).
The conclusion that f(SiC2) increases with wind density is based on only three sources, one of which (II Lup) was fit with just two transitions and has no uncertainty estimate.
